A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and figure relocation.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix F report original simulations comparing GD and SpecGD, including population dynamics, learning-rate sensitivity, and power-law covariance experiments.

after.justification: The original simulations remain, supplemented by a power-law parameter sweep and a perturbed-MNIST classification experiment in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The SpecGD polar-gradient update, phase-retrieval model, and objective remain unchanged. The added ReLU network tests the existing optimizer in another setting rather than introducing a new proposed method.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates synthetic phase retrieval under spiked and power-law Gaussian covariances. v2 additionally evaluates binary MNIST classification, digits 4 versus 9, using a ReLU network and perturbed image inputs, substantially extending task and data coverage.

E2.justification: Muon becomes an evaluated comparator alongside GD and SpecGD in the new power-law sweep and MNIST experiment, Figures 9–10. v1 discusses Muon but evaluates only GD and SpecGD; the retained comparisons keep their original participants.

E3.justification: The new MNIST evaluation introduces standardized 784-dimensional inputs, a controlled Gaussian nuisance spike, full-batch ReLU training, and test accuracy plotted over 2000 epochs at tau = 200. Figure 9 also introduces an exponent-by-learning-rate sweep. Existing experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: Figure 9 adds a focused sensitivity analysis varying the power-law exponent and learning rate beyond v1's fixed-exponent demonstration. Figure 10 adds a controlled nuisance-perturbation test on MNIST. Earlier population-dynamics and learning-rate analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. The added curves and heatmaps introduce no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Existing experimental plots retain their results after relocation and renumbering. New Figure 9 shows broader high-alignment regions for SpecGD and Muon than GD as anisotropy increases. Figure 10 adds MNIST accuracy trajectories ending around 90–95% for the spectral methods versus roughly 50% for GD. These are new results, not improvements over v1 under matched settings.

T1.justification: The assumptions, Theorems 4.1–4.3, reduced dynamics, and proofs in Appendices A–E are substantively unchanged. Definition punctuation and corrected GD notation do not alter the mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about invariant-manifold reduction, anisotropy-driven GD misalignment, and SpecGD's faster alignment. The new experiments support these claims without redefining the central contributions.

C2.justification: The new MNIST discussion interprets similar SpecGD and Muon behavior as evidence that spectral normalization mitigates nuisance anisotropy beyond phase retrieval. The discussion of improved alignment despite erratic power-law losses already appeared in v1 Appendix F and is largely relocated.

D1.justification: Appendix F newly documents MNIST flattening and standardization, construction of a nuisance direction orthogonal to the class-mean difference, Gaussian perturbations, and full-batch training; Figure 10 specifies tau = 200. These are limited additional implementation details, with network width and optimizer hyperparameters still unspecified for this experiment.

R1.justification: v2 adds Lau, Long, and Su's Polargrad work to the discussion of optimization guarantees. Other prominent reference changes update publication metadata for existing works, while the paper's positioning relative to earlier research remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar, terminology, and notation edits, moves the existing power-law interpretation into Section 6, and adds short descriptions of the new experiments. The main narrative and proof-appendix organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch to a two-column conference layout with revised typography and headers. Figure 3 and v1 Figure 8, now Figure 4, move into the main text; other figures are renumbered, and new Figures 9–10 display the added experiments.

improvement.justification: Figures 9–10 strengthen the empirical connection between the idealized SpecGD analysis, Muon, and a nonquadratic real-data task while retaining the original results and proofs. The gain is limited: MNIST uses one reported perturbation strength, and the new experiments lack run uncertainty and some important training details.
